title: Marfan syndrome? Something else?
selftext:

I am wondering if this my health anxiety acting up or something I should bring up to my doctor. 

About 18 months ago, my dad had triple bypass heart surgery at 64. He hadn’t had any heart issues prior, but has been a heavy drinker most of his life and definitely wasn’t eating a healthy diet. He is 5’10” and has flat feet and longish fingers. 

I have been skinny my whole life and have a few smaller indicators of hyper mobility, my fingers are kind of long and skinny and I have skinny wrists. I’ve never had any joint dislocations, but I did have some back issues last year. I’ve never had any eye issues and had crowded teeth, but so did my mom. 

I don’t want to sound stupid and like a hypochondriac by bringing this up to my doctor, but I would like to know if my dad’s heart issue could be genetic.

title: Friend has been on heavy medication for 4+ years now with no end in sight... becoming skeptical.
selftext:
So as the title states I have a close childhood friend who I have known since I was 6 years old. Grew up across the street from each other and had a good ole time all the way up through high school.

Cut to us being off in college, about halfway through our first year my said friend goes home in early spring for anxiety and depression and begins taking heavy doses of prescription medication. One medication that he refers to frequently is Ativan.

He is the youngest of three siblings and his mom wears the pants in the household and has always been quite controlling. Around when he left for school his parents moved 40 min away to a far more secluded part of town so when I am home I don’t really see him anymore.

With all of that being said my friend is barely even the same person now. His speech is heavily slurred and he can barely produce coherent thoughts that make sense. Can’t drive, doesn’t work a job, no video games to play with our friend group like he used to. He mainly just sits at home drugged up.

For the last 3 years he has been saying they are going to ween him off of the drugs and he will get back to normal. But it has now been 4 years since he started taking the drugs and there is no end in sight. I really just feel sorry for him at this point and knowing his mom I worry they are holding him back so they can keep him in the house where they can care for him intentionally.

I don't know maybe I’m just overreacting or paranoid but my childhood friend is a drugged up mess and he’s got nothing going for him now and something seems really off about the situation.

Anyone here know someone who took heavy doses of Ativan and got off it? Or someone who could reassure me that this is even slightly normal? I mean 4 years at home with no driving, not much interaction beyond doctors visits and family, and just heavy drugs that keep his brain like a slushy.

title: Diagnosed with probable spider bites, multiple new spots started appearing 7 days later, along with different type of rash not present at last doctor visit. Not sure what questions to ask the doc, and is it ok to wait until Monday?
selftext:
5 year old Caucasian male

36 pounds, 42 inches

Tramcinolone ointment, prescribed for this rash.

No medical history other than birth at 34 weeks gestation.

No smoke exposure. Resides in Utah.

Multiple family members on maternal and paternal side with autoimmune diseases (RA, mixed connective tissue disease, T1D). Patient's sibling has Type 1 diabetes and celiac disease.

 [https://imgur.com/a/kPBbhfq](https://imgur.com/a/kPBbhfq) 

7 days ago patient developed one spot on each shin. Both started as pink dots with a thin pink ring around them. Throughout the next day or two they became more red, purplish in the center, and looked generally angry. Swelling about 3 inches wide around each spot that was not discolored.  Itching present. He's been good about not scratching, but did cry a few times about it. On Day 3 he was seen by his pediatrician who thought they were consistent with spider bites, and expected them to improve, and they did not look infected. At their largest they were a little smaller than a quarter. They started improving synchronously, still present today but looking better and only mildly itchy at times. Today (Day 7) a few new spots appeared in the same dot with ring pattern and are already progressing to the darker, angrier looking spot. One on the left leg, one on the right foot, and possibly one on the left foot (this one might be a mosquito bite but I'm not sure). I also noticed for the first time today a different rash on both lower legs. Pencil tip size spots, they look mostly flat but I can feel them when I touch them. The left leg has swelling around the new spots and there is mild pain when flexing toes towards knees. He is limping because of swelling near the spot on the right foot. Temperature 98.4. I've washed bedding and vacuumed, etc.

His doctor is out until Monday, so I left a message for her to call back. Is this something that can wait until Monday? And should we be investigating things other than spider bites?

title: Doctor ordered brain and neck MRI. Does this sound familiar?
selftext:
32. Female. 190 lbs. 5’4”. Non smoker, rarely any alcohol. History of bulging cervical disc, sinus tachycardia, normal BP (110/70 up to 120/80). I’m prescribed metroperol as needed for heart palpitations and I haven’t used it in months. 

I started working out regularly in January. I noticed if I laid flat on my back or did plank/downward dog/push ups it felt like there was a ton of pressure in my head. It made me lightheaded. No pain. I emailed my doctor and she said it could be my bulging disc or something else. Now I get the pressure in those positions or if I sit at my computer chair for work or stand up too quickly. 

I remember having this issue in college and my doctor ordered an MRI but insurance denied it and so I moved on. Eventually the pressure went away or I didn’t notice it as much. Now that I work out 4-5 times a week, I can really notice it. And now it’s started happening in newer times and positions. I feel the pressure kind of all over. Sinuses, side of head, ears. I went to the eye doctor and confirmed great vision and no swelling of optical nerve. 

I went to the doctor’s office today and she ordered head and neck MRI with contrast. I’m waiting on the date. She said she thinks it’s the bulging disc because it is “positional” but wants to rule out hydrocephalus and brain tumor and something about spinal fluid. 

I’ll be real. I’m a mom to an awesome 3 year old and snuggly 1 year old. I have been terrified all day. I can’t get it out of my head that she said brain tumor. Has anyone heard of these symptoms before? Does this sound like a brain tumor or something more benign? I just don’t want to leave my kids without a mom and now I’m envisioning the worst. I guess I was just hoping these symptoms seemed similar to anything you all have seen to maybe brace myself. Thank you so much.

selftext:

title: 21F, heavy bleeding on early period + stinging breast pain
selftext:
Good morning.  I am 21F, 5’1” and 120lbs on average. I apologize—this is going to be gross and TMI. It’s 3am and I’m worried sick, so I can’t really be bothered with feeling embarrassed. For the last two days, I have been experiencing lower abdominal cramping akin to constipation. I assumed I had eaten something bad and it would pass on its own. 

However, as I was eating dinner this past evening (about 7 hours ago), the pain became worse, and I felt a large amount of fluid exit my body, which prompted me to go to the restroom to see what was going on.  To my surprise, I had started my period two weeks early and it was much heavier than I had ever seen.  In a matter of seconds, the blood had soaked through to the seat of my pants, if that gives you an idea of how bad it was.  I put a pad in in the interim. I walked 15 min back to my apartment and washed my clothes and used another pad (because the first was already moderately full), which filled quickly. I am experiencing a good deal of cramping and am about to be on my fourth pad in 7 hours. I am no stranger to cramping (I usually have pretty painful periods, it’s just a fact of life for me), but the amount of bright red blood leaving my body is concerning to me.  

I distracted myself with some games for a few hours and found afterwards that my breasts were stinging/searing with pain.

I have also noticed I’ve been carrying around about 5 extra pounds the past couple months and feeling fat and bad about myself, and I feel smaller since the bleeding started.  This particular symptom could be psychological.  Other from what I mentioned, this has been fairly normal.  I had routine PMS for about a week that I didn’t think was PMS, given that I wasn’t expecting a period. Irritability, depressed mood, increased hunger, weight gain, the like.

For some context—About half the time I get periods, I have moderate to severe cramping, fatigue and weakness of my limbs, and what I call my period fever, which is a heightened body temp with sweats. Additionally, I have historically had irregular periods, and my last few have been lighter and less painful than usual. I have been having periods for ten years. I also believe I have ovarian cysts due to interperiod bleeding and what I believe to have been painful ruptures, but I cannot medically confirm this as of now. Scared of the ultrasound, I guess.

So, my question is this: do I go to urgent care in the morning? I don’t know if this could be a sign of something dire, or if it’s just my uterus throwing a fit as usual. I’m sorry this was long. Thank you for taking the time of day to read this.

title: I went down the Chronic Lyme path, because I don’t know where else to go. Is there another path?
selftext:
This will all be in relation to my husband.

Caucasian
Male
33 years old

March 2020, Husband has taken up trail running, we live in western Montana. After pushing himself a little too hard on a run, he came home complaining of right leg IT band pain. Repeatedly came back even after refraining from any running for a month and a half and starting back very slowly. Also experienced foot pain that he attributed to plantar fasciitis. but he has very flat feet and an old ankle injury from a motorcycle wreck so I don’t know if that is relevant.

May 2020: he comes to me with what had been a VERY engorged tick that had been in his beard for roughly 3 days after an overnight backpacking trip. I urge him to see a doctor but he does not. The spot develops a large, sensitive lump that was warm to the touch and swollen for a while. A knot remained in the spot for several weeks. He continues his running, and soon develops pain is his left leg IT band. Foot pain is still very persistent and bad. By June 2020 he has developed hip pain in both hips and cannot continue running due to the multitude of issues. We are very outdoorsy people and most anything we did came with a ton of pain as the consequence. 

Fast forward to December 2020: he has seen his primary doctor who noted there seemed to be inflammation in his connective tissues but not his joints directly. He begins six (maybe eight I don’t remember) weeks of physical therapy. The IT band pain has migrated to the back of his knees (his hamstring connectors) and PT attributed this to his glutes not being engaged properly. There was zero improvement after PT. 

Our timeline gets blurry after this, but pain migrates from hamstring connectors, to groin, to elbows, he has bouts of carpal tunnel… he would always note that it wasn’t joint pain it was tissue pain. I sent him to an orthopedist for his hips thinking he had an impingement. They said nothing was wrong and his hips looked great. Primary doc sends him to a rheumatologist in Feb 2021. Tests for RA, Schogrens, ankylosis spondylitis, Ehlers Danos, and a few other things that are ruled out. He leaves with a vague diagnosis of hyper mobility with no follow up from the rheumatologist or primary doc. 

From Feb through July he basically just suffers. Nothing helps alleviate the connective tissue pain, activity makes it worse. By July I have discovered the path of Lyme disease. We visit a naturopath Lyme literate doctor who runs a very basic spot test for borrelia and bartonella. Both negative but he treats based on clinical diagnosis. At no point were we pressured or told to do anything we were not comfortable with. He is on the normal amount of Doxycycline that is normally used for Lyme along with azithromycin for four months and spent one month on Malarone for babesia but was taken off of it by naturopath because of liver enzyme levels. Naturopath stops all antibiotics and says he does not believe this can be attributed to Lyme and that the lack of reaction or real improvement suggests he does not have Lyme. The joint pain and bottom of foot pain persists and worsens after stopping antibiotics and remains bad even now, with intermittent days of feeling ok. Some days the hips are awful, today specifically his feet are killing him. 

He has also developed digestive issues in the last two months. It started with small amounts of food making him feel disgustingly full. Progressed to constant burping even after not eating for 14+ hours. There is no constipation or diarrhea but he describes his stomach as constantly feeling “blech” like it would when you have a massive hangover. There is no vomiting. He had a gallbladder attack about a month ago where it was twinging with worsening pain for about 24 hours. The feeling passed but he still had an ultrasound done which showed no stones or sludge and his liver and kidney looked fine. This was done at our local hospital and they reported nothing of concern. He does not eat consistently because the moment he does he feels gross. 

So here we are. Connective tissue pain has never resolved, has actually worsened. He has developed digestive issues and had problems with his gallbladder. His mental state has changed from a very level headed and calm person to an irritable and depressed person. He has a lot of memory issues and forgets names and words often. 

He is 5’8” weighing around 151 lbs, was lifting weights and working out up until he became unable to eat a lot due to these digestive issues and knew he wasn’t taking in enough calories. The man is always hydrated, true r/hydrohomies member. The weight lifting had to be restricted to upper body because the leg workouts affected his knees too badly. His elbows would hurt occasionally and he did develop more issues with his hands. His dad was an Olympic weight lifter and owned a gym so I am confident in his form and routine being good. 

His blood tests show very elevated eosinophils, slightly elevated liver enzymes, and normal thyroid levels. Stool test showed no parasites and celiac was negative. H. Pylori was negative. ANA, CRP and fecal calprotectin were normal.  

So where do we go from here? I have taken him off all supplements I had from the chronic Lyme community. He took Pepcid AC and his stomach felt normal for two days, we eliminated red meat which helped his stomach for about a week. Both stopped helping. Chronic Lyme and co infections felt like an answer but I see the science saying it’s not. We need a different path before we crumble. So what do you see?

title: [23F] Hundres of pimples on the forehead if not on medication
selftext:
Hello AskDocs, i´m really in the need of help.

First: English is my second language so my text might not be perfect.

Second: This post is about my girlfriend, she asked me to post it here, because she isn´t on reddit.

Before someone asks: We are healthy, doing sports 3-4 times a week, eat enough and healthy, only drink water (alot of water), normal weight for our height. We work both in offices, around 39 hours a week. 

Lets go: My girlfriend had a bad problem with pimples on her forehead through her puberty, but not like normal, after puberty these wouldn´t leave. She started to fight them at the age of 13 with serveral cremes, pills, visits at the doctor, everything you can imagine and nothing helped. Now she is 23, living with me in our apartment. Two years ago, she got a medication called Isogalen prescribed from her dermatologist. She takes it almost everyday. It makes the pimples go away by drying out the skin and body extremly. When she doesn´t take them a few days/weeks, over hundred of very tiny pimples start to spread on her forehead. The problem is that Isogalen isn´t healthy in every way to her body. She has to take a pregancy test everytime, to get a new pack. She lost a good amount of eyesight over the last to years because of the pills. It even has some negative effects on her stress at work. Even the dermatologists are out of ther knowledge after her visit yesterday. Maybe some of you, around the world know a medication oder creme or whatever, that she can try to use. 

I really hope that someone knows something we can try or even just look after. Thank you in advance.

PS: We are from Germany.
